paragraphs: Apple’s ‘Surprise and shine’ event is set for September 9, but the company already surprised us this week by launching new products in late August. Here’s why that rare move could signal big things coming at the September event.
If you follow Apple closely, you start to notice patterns in the company’s calendar year.
New products typically launch around March, then June brings WWDC and software unveilings, followed by a big September event, and often some October launches too.
While it’s not unusual to see smaller products debut via press releases throughout the rest of the year, one thing is exceptionally rare: a late August product launch.
Over the past 10 years, Apple has only once launched new hardware in August. That lone product was the iMac in 2020—but it debuted early in the month on August 4.
Why don’t late August launches happen? Because having a September event right around the corner means new hardware would typically be held until then.
In fact, the 2020 iMac isn’t even a fair example of defying this trend. Due to COVID, Apple pushed its iPhone event that year to October instead of September.

And yet, despite a wealth of evidence that August product launches don’t ever happen, this week Apple surprised us by launching new Mac mini and Mac Studio models just two weeks before its September 9 event.
